newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex details expected regional 1997 production. [Corrected 7:57 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Pemex details expected regional 1997 production. [Corrected 7:57 gmt]

text.p: Petroleos Mexicanos expects to boost 1997 crude oil production 7.7 percent, focusing on extraction in Mexico's northeast marine region (corrects from "...northeast Mexico extraction...") the state-owned oil and gas company said in a report Wednesday.

According to its budget proposal before the congressional energy commission, Pemex crude production in 1997 should increase by 196,000 barrel per day (bpd) in the northeast, compared to 12,000 bpd in the southeast marine region (corrects from "...in the southeast..."), 10,000 bpd in the south and 4,000 bpd in the north.
Pemex chief Adrian Lajous has said crude oil production should increase 7.7 percent in 1997 from the previous year to 3.083 million (bpd).
Of crude oil produced, 55 percent will be exported and 44 percent destined to refining and the remainder left to inventory.

Natural gas production is expected to jump 8.4 percent next year, according to company estimates. In the south an extra 188 million cubic feet is estimated, with an additional 101 million cubic feet in the northern region, 58 million cubic feet in the northeast and 6 million cubic feet in the southeast.
Half of dry gas sales will be used by Pemex, the company said, with 46 percent sold internally and four percent exported.
Pemex expects internal sales to rise slightly in most petroleum products, for a total 3.0 percent increase.
Company predictions for 1997 expect domestic natural gas sales to rise 5.1 percent.

Industrial combustibles should rise 1.5 percent to 672,000 bpd, according to the estimates, while fuel oil sales are predicted to fall 0.6 percent to 415,000 barrels per day. A decline in fuel oil sales could reflect a conscious shift away from the more polluting fuel.
Pemex also estimates five percent higher diesel sales to 253,000 bpd in 1997, and an eight percent rise in turbine fuel sales to 49,000 mpd.l

Domestic sales of petroleum products, natural gas and petrochemicals are expected (corrects from "...sales of petrochemicals are expected...") to increase to 167 billion pesos in 1997, up 4.2 percent, compared with larger sales increases in past years.

Mexico's oil and gas monopoly plans to sell a minority stake in the country's 61 petrochemical plants, and allow private ownership of new plants. Pemex has said it hopes to attract new capital to the industry, which outside critics say is unprofitable due to insufficient investment.
--Timna Tanners, Mexico City newsroom +525 728 7903 (c) Reuters Limited 1996
